subject: BAA & POC: PHI handling boundaries and deployment options
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Chen <l.chen@medisys.com>, security@medisys.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BAA & POC: PHI handling boundaries and deployment options

Laura / InfoSec — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can scope the POC and surface the right controls for your security team.

Recap from Redwood side:
- SOC 2 status: we maintain SOC 2 Type II reporting; we can provide the auditor letter under NDA.
- BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployment modes. Our standard hosted public API is not approved for PHI unless we provision an isolated, contractual Dedicated tenancy (we can discuss).
- PHI handling: for a short POC we typically recommend either (a) synthetic/de-identified data, or (b) tokenized PHI with customer-side key management. Avoid sending raw PHI to hosted multi-tenant endpoints.

Specific asks for MediSys POC:
1) Can you confirm whether the POC will use synthetic/de-identified records or if you expect to send live PHI? If the latter, please confirm whether MediSys legal can run a BAA concurrently.
2) Does InfoSec require KMS/HSM integration (customer-managed keys) for the POC? We support KMS integration for Dedicated and Private.
3) Any gating controls we should include in the SOW: e.g., IP allowlist, network peering, log retention windows, or MDR/SIEM integration points?

Attachments: I attached our initial security questionnaire (PDF) and a minimal POC SOW template for your review.

Next steps we propose:
- InfoSec completes the attached questionnaire and returns it to us (we can fill gaps as needed).
- If you intend to send live PHI for the POC, legal to confirm BAA timing and Redwood to provision a Dedicated POC pool (estimate: 5 business days after BAA & payment).
- Schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to align on sample records and telemetry.

Thanks — I can be flexible with times.

— Michael Grant
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: MediSys_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, POC_SOW_draft.docx

From: Laura Chen <l.chen@medisys.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: BAA & POC: PHI handling boundaries and deployment options

Thanks, Michael — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from InfoSec / program side: 

- For the POC we prefer to avoid sending live PHI if possible. We can provide a representative synthetic dataset for initial validation. If the POC needs behavioral parity with live records we may request a small, encrypted sample later.
- BAA: MediSys will need a BAA signed before any sustained live-PHI exchange (production). For a short, one-off sample we can consider an interim agreement, but legal needs to review.
- SOC 2: please include the auditor contact or a copy of the report under NDA; that will expedite our review.
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys (KMS) for any environment that will see live PHI.
- Networking: IP allowlist and private peering are both likely requirements for production. For the POC, an allowlist and restricted logging/retention is sufficient.

I'll have our security engineer (security@medisys.com) complete the attached questionnaire and return it by Friday. Can you send a redline-friendly SOW and a proposed kickoff window (we're in PST)?

Laura Chen
Head of Product Security
MediSys Health

Subject: Internal: Notes on MediSys asks (SOC 2, BAA, POC)

Folks — quick internal summary and suggested language to send back: 

- SOC 2: Confirmed Type II in place; we should offer to deliver the SOC 2 report under NDA and flag any exceptions in the report that relate to third-party subservice organizations. Action: ops to prepare redacted report and NDA boilerplate.
- BAA: Standard Redwood BAA is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments. For production with PHI we require either Dedicated reserved capacity or Private (VPC/on-prem) with our BAA. For a time-boxed POC, we can provision a dedicated POC pool under a short-term invoice and include a scoped BAA addendum; legal should review.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. For hosted public API we offer encryption at rest and in transit but do not expose key material to customers.
- POC recommendations: use synthetic data initially; if a small live sample is required, require tokenization + KMS, limit retention to 7 days, disable prefix caching, and enable aggressive log scrubbing. Provision an IP allowlist and optional private peering (if they want lower latency).

Action items before sending to MediSys:
1) Rishi — send a redline-friendly SOW with the POC scope and pricing (include 5 business day provisioning estimate for Dedicated POC).
2) Ops — prepare SOC 2 under NDA and confirm auditor contact.
3) Legal — draft BAA addendum for short-term POC and standard BAA for production.

I'll draft a short answer thread we can send to Laura that calls out these points and proposes two kickoff slots next Tues/Wed morning PST.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

    * Dedicated POC pool (short-term reserved capacity) with customer KMS integration and IP allowlist, or
    * Private deployment (VPC) for full isolation.
- Provisioning estimate for a Dedicated POC: 5 business days after BAA and purchase order; Private deployments vary by customer environment.

Proposed kickoff: Tue Apr 17 10:00 AM PST or Wed Apr 18 09:30 AM PST — please confirm which works for your team.
